Q: How to find and delete duplicate rows in SQL while keeping the newest entry? A:

Try something like this:

WITH CTE AS (
SELECT
    [id]
  , ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY [user_id] ORDER BY [created_at] DESC) AS RowNumber
FROM
    [dbo].[users]
)
DELETE
FROM CTE
WHERE RowNumber > 1;

Change the DELETE to a SELECT * if you want to check the output before you run it as a delete.

Q: Best API documentation tool for a multi-service architecture (Swagger/OpenAPI vs Redoc vs Postman)? A:

There are a lot of choices for API docs tool such as the company I founded, Jamdesk, especially if you're comfortable with managing markdown and MDX (gives you the most flexibility). Here are somethings to consider:

  • Are you going to be use AI agents to maintain/build the docs? I do with human review/fixing before publishing. If so, this is where MDX comes into play - the AI agents can use those tool's CLI to update, review and publish.

  • Do you want self updating docs? So you write and API or update and now you have an API docs page. Don't however, just publish. Do the human review or you're going to have sucky docs.

  • How many team members do you want to add - pricing varies from $ to $$$$ per team member.

  • Do you want hosted of self-hosted?

Some others to consider are Mintlify, Readme, Gitbook, Jamdesk, and Docusaurus (self-hosted).*

Q: As a working software engineer, should I prioritize DSA, System Design, or AI/ML for career growth? A:

As someone in DS/DE who has been at both startups and bigger companies for a few years, I have found that System Design and AI/ML are the most useful. Since I am not a proper SE, I don't want to speak on their behalf too much, but I would probably de-emphasize DSA. AI can probably help with implementing standard algorithms, though you should understand the fundamentals well enough to be able to validate and QA its code, as well as provide guidance to AI and understand broader architectural decisions you're making when building out a codebase, internal library, etc.

There's some facets to AI/ML too - while I personally believe that understanding basics of ML (linear algebra, neural networks, and various ML architectures) are good for critical thinking and deeper understanding, it's probably not strictly necessary to be able to understand the mathematics as deeply as before. If you want to be practical, you can learn about the state-of-the-art AI/ML architectures at a deep enough level that you know the use cases and tradeoffs for different architectures without necessarily having to know all the mathematics behind how it works. You should probably conceptually understand linear regression, vanilla NNs, decision trees, and transformer architectures to name a few.

Q: The infamous java.sql.SQLException: No suitable driver found A:

I won't duplicate the already existing answers, they explain very well most of the cases when this error appears, but I want to share my experience with the same error. In my case this error was caused by using a wrong Java version for an existing project. I didn't pay attention to look for the project's Java version and it turns out that the project was using Java 8 and I was trying to run it with Java 17. I've tried all of the answers and solutions but nothing helped until I changed the Java version. So this is another scenario, apart from the already mentioned, where this error may appear.
